intro: Four image-led steps separate John Glasgow's identity and widow from the damaged inventory, the procurator's request and the court confirmation. Heavy show-through is visible and is treated as a source limit, not silently repaired. National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court CC14/5/12, images 67-68, Crown copyright; accessed through Scotland's People wills and testaments.

steps.title: 1. Identify Quothquan, the February death and the widow
steps.page_label: National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court CC14/5/12, image 67; Crown copyright
steps.alt: 1. Original manuscript crop naming John Glasgow in Quothquan, Libberton parish, and Jonet as relict and executrix dative.
steps.original: umq[uhi]le John Glasgow in Quothquan within the paroch of Libberton ... deceist intestat in the moneth of ffebruary ... Jonet [Kinnie?] relict and executrix dative
steps.reading: The late John Glasgow in Quothquan, Libberton parish, died intestate in February 1685. Jonet [Kinnie?], his widow, served as executrix dative.
steps.explanation: Box 1 follows the deceased's name into Quothquan. Box 2 carries the parish wording. Box 3 contains the intestacy and February phrase. Box 4 contains Jonet's name and the adjoining role words. Relict proves widowhood; executrix dative describes a court-appointed estate office. The surname remains qualified because show-through crosses its minims.
steps.proves: John's record-defined residence and death month, plus Jonet's explicit widow and executrix roles.
steps.does_not_prove: It does not name a child or parent, and it does not bridge John to the 1608 Mid Calder baptism.
steps.confidence: High for identity, locality, month/year and roles; moderate-low for Jonet's surname.

features: John begins with a tall black J whose lower curve returns into the short o-h-n group.
Glasgow has a broad looped capital G and a final w formed by two pointed strokes.
Quothquan shows two separate q descenders, one at the opening and one in the second syllable.
analysis.comparison: John Glasgow recurs in the procurator's clause in step 3, helping distinguish name strokes from show-through.
analysis.uncertainty: The name and Quothquan are secure; several overlying reverse-page strokes cross the line.

features: Within begins with a wide w followed by a row of narrow minims in ithin.
Paroch contains a tall h ascender at its end.
Libberton begins with an upright looped L and has two tall strokes in bb.
analysis.comparison: The following line adds the presbytery of Lanark, keeping this a geographic designation.
analysis.uncertainty: Libberton is legible despite bleed-through; the exact spelling is preserved.

analysis.reading: deceist intestat in the moneth of ffebruary
analysis.expansion: died intestate in the month of February
features: Intestat contains a long s-like vertical and two tall t strokes crossed near their tops.
Ffebruary begins with a doubled initial f convention, both strokes extending below the baseline.
The final y has a long descending tail that curves back toward the word.
analysis.comparison: The 1685 year appears on the next line; step 4 supplies the later March court date.
analysis.uncertainty: The month is clear; no February day is stated.

features: Jonet begins with a long initial J descending below the line.
Relict has a tall l and final t crossed by a light horizontal stroke.
Executrix begins with an enlarged loop and ends in a distinct x-shaped crossing.
analysis.comparison: Jonet's appointment is carried into the court confirmation in step 4.
analysis.uncertainty: Relict and executrix dative are secure. Reverse-page ink crosses the surname, so Kinnie remains provisional.

steps.title: 2. Treat the dark middle as an inventory with source damage
steps.page_label: National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court CC14/5/12, image 67; Crown copyright
steps.alt: 2. Original manuscript crop of John's heavily obscured livestock, crop and clothing inventory.
steps.original: Inventar ... Item two kyne ... the abulzement of the defuncts bodie ... Summa of the Inventar
steps.reading: The inventory includes livestock, farm produce or fodder, household/farm goods and the deceased's clothing, but most exact quantities and prices remain obscured.
steps.explanation: Box 1 is the large heading. Box 2 pulls the clearest livestock phrase. Box 3 marks the clothing valuation, and Box 4 the total heading. The heavy dark lines crossing these entries are show-through and overwriting; the walkthrough therefore stops short of invented item totals.
steps.proves: The estate included livestock and ordinary farm/household property.
steps.does_not_prove: The damaged list cannot support exact wealth calculations or family relationships.
steps.confidence: High for the inventory structure and broad classes; low to moderate for individual quantities and valuations.

features: The initial I is a very tall black stroke extending below the baseline into a broad curve.
The middle n-v-e sequence is compressed into alternating thick and thin joins.
The final r is short and hooked upward.
analysis.comparison: This large display heading contrasts with the smaller same word in Summa of the Inventar below.
analysis.uncertainty: The heading is clear even though reverse-page writing crosses it.

features: Item begins with a tall upright I and a compact tem group.
The w in two is formed from two pointed downstrokes.
Kyne has a long y descender and a final e turning upward.
analysis.comparison: Geillis's earlier hand writes the related cattle word ky in step 3 of her walkthrough.
analysis.uncertainty: Two kyne is legible; the milk/follower description and price alongside it are less secure.

analysis.expansion: clothing/personal apparel of the deceased's body
features: Abulzement begins with an open capital A and a tall looped b.
Defuncts has a long descending f and a tightly joined unct sequence.
Bodie ends with a clearly separated i dot and a final e curl.
analysis.comparison: This conventional personal-apparel item follows the agricultural property entries.
analysis.uncertainty: The phrase is substantially legible; its appended valuation is obscured.

features: Summa begins with a broad capital S whose lower curve reaches under the word.
The double m appears as a run of narrow minims.
Inventar retains a taller initial than the surrounding words despite the darker ink crossing it.
analysis.comparison: The total heading closes the inventory before the separate debt account.
analysis.uncertainty: The words are legible; the numeric sum at the right is not dependable.

steps.title: 3. Read William Wilkie as an officer, not a relative
steps.page_label: National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court CC14/5/12, image 67; Crown copyright
steps.alt: 3. Original manuscript crop beginning I William Wilkie procurator fiscal and naming the late John Glasgow.
steps.original: I William Wilkie procurator fiscall of this court ... goods and geir of the said umq[uhi]le John Glasgow
steps.reading: William Wilkie appears as procurator fiscal in the court request concerning the late John Glasgow's estate.
steps.explanation: Box 1 is the officer's personal name and Box 2 his title. Box 3 returns to John Glasgow as the deceased whose goods are in process. The role label controls interpretation: William is conducting procedure, not being introduced as kin.
steps.proves: William Wilkie's official participation in the estate process.
steps.does_not_prove: It does not make William Wilkie a brother, son or other relative of John or Jonet.
steps.confidence: High for William Wilkie and procurator fiscal; moderate for the surrounding legal formula.

features: William begins with a very large W built from deep pointed strokes and a leftward entry flourish.
The doubled l rises as two tall parallel ascenders.
Wilkie repeats the pointed W but ends with a small dotted i and curled e.
analysis.comparison: The second W is smaller but shares the same angular downstroke pattern as the first.
analysis.uncertainty: The name is clear; reverse-page text intersects but does not replace its strokes.

features: Procurator opens with a tall looped p whose descender falls below the baseline.
The c and r are open, narrow forms separated by visible pen lifts.
Fiscall contains a long s and ends with two tall l ascenders.
analysis.comparison: Unlike relict and executrix in step 1, this title belongs to a court officer.
analysis.uncertainty: The title is clear; spelling fiscall is literal.

features: Umqle is heavily abbreviated, with the q descender carrying much of the form.
John begins with the same tall descending J seen in step 1.
Glasgow ends in the same sharply pointed w as the opening name.
analysis.comparison: The repeated John Glasgow form confirms that this clause still concerns the same deceased.
analysis.uncertainty: The name is secure; the conventional expansion of umqle is editorially supplied.

steps.title: 4. Separate Jonet's oath from William Watson's caution
steps.page_label: National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court CC14/5/12, image 68; Crown copyright
steps.alt: 4. Original manuscript crop of the 25 March 1685 court proceeding, Jonet's oath and William Watson's caution.
steps.original: At Carnwath the 25 day of March 1685 ... compeired personallie Jonet [Kinnie?] ... William Watson ... cautioner ... goods ... furthcoming to all parties haveand interes
steps.reading: At Carnwath on 25 March 1685, Jonet personally presented and swore the inventory; William Watson acted as cautioner for the estate goods.
steps.explanation: Box 1 is the dated court opening. Box 2 follows Jonet's personal appearance and oath context. Box 3 isolates William Watson with the cautioner wording, and Box 4 follows the guarantee that goods be forthcoming to interested parties. These are distinct procedural acts, not family descriptions.
steps.proves: The proceeding date, Jonet's personal estate oath and William Watson's security role.
steps.does_not_prove: It does not identify William Watson as kin and adds no child or parent for John.
steps.confidence: High for the date and role distinction; moderate for Jonet's surname and William's place designation.

marks.label: At Carnwath the 25 day of March 1685

analysis.reading: At Carnwath the 25 day of March 1685
features: Carnwath begins with a large open C followed by connected arnwath strokes.
The Arabic 25 is separated from day by a small gap.
March has a broad M and a final h ascender rising above the line.
analysis.comparison: The same 25 March date is docketed on image 67; this full clause identifies the proceeding place.
analysis.uncertainty: Carnwath and the date are clear; this is a court date, not John's death date.

features: Compeired begins with an open capital C and contains a long p descender.
Personallie has a tall long-s form and two adjacent l ascenders.
Jonet begins with the familiar long descending J at the right end of the line.
analysis.comparison: The same given name and J form appear beside relict and executrix in step 1.
analysis.uncertainty: Jonet is secure; her surname follows elsewhere and remains uncertain.

features: William opens with the same deep pointed W construction seen in William Wilkie on image 67.
Watson has a distinct tall W and a long s before the final on.
Cautioner begins with a large open C and ends with a short raised r.
analysis.comparison: William Wilkie in step 3 is procurator fiscal; William Watson here has the different role cautioner.
analysis.uncertainty: The name and cautioner role are readable; the intervening place designation is not.

marks.label: furthcoming to all parties haveand interes

analysis.reading: furthcoming to all parties haveand interes
analysis.expansion: made available to all parties having an interest
features: Furthcoming begins with a tall f descending below the line.
Parties has a p descender and a long s at the end.
Interes closes with a long final s-like stroke after the compact tere sequence.
analysis.comparison: This obligation explains the practical purpose of Watson's cautioner role in Box 3.
analysis.uncertainty: The core phrase is legible; adjoining legal words are obscured by show-through.
